# 2 Baruch Chapter 44 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Third Fast and Vision

---

**44:1** And-I-Baruch answered and-said to-the-elders:

**44:2** Hear [me], all-of-you-elders; and-hearken [to me], all-of-you-who-are-gathered [here]:

**44:3** You-know that-our-fathers-in-times-past left-the-law; and-on-account-of-this [evil]-things-came-upon-them and-upon-us.

**44:4** But-the-hope-of-those-who-have-kept-the-commandments of-the-Mighty-One — the-reward-[of-their-hope]-will-not-fail; and-their-portion [will remain] when-the-times-will-fail.

**44:5** For-the-time-of-the-world-will-pass-away, and-its-glory-will-grow-old, and-everything-beautiful-in-it will-turn-[to]-decay; and-the-proud-ones will-become-as-if-they-were-not.

**44:6** And-those-who-trust-in-[their]-wealth will-be-like-those-who-have-passed-away; and-those-who-have-dominion-over-[others]-will-wail and-be-put-to-shame.

**44:7** For-the-things-which-are-to-come are-things-of-great-worth and-great-greatness, and-those-things-which-are-passing-away are-small-and-fleeting.

**44:8** All-those-therefore who-have-hoped-in-the-Anointed-One-who-was-to-come — [all]-those-will-be-in-gladness; and-those-who-were-not-in-the-number-of-the-people-of-knowledge — those-will-be-destroyed.

**44:9** For-the-hope-of-those-who-trusted-in-their-heart-[in]-the-law-will-not-perish; it-will-not-fail.

**44:10** And-the-lamp-of-this-world: how-long-will-it-shine? And-when-will-the-darkness-thereof-be-destroyed, which-at-present-covers-everything?

**44:11** And-for-what-reason-does-the-beauty-of-the-earth-grow-old? And-for-what-reason will-its-strength-be-corrupted? And-when-will-it-be-that-the-Mighty-One-[himself] will-come in-glory to-judge-all-the-people who-dwell-upon-the-earth?

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Syriac Codex Ambrosianus. Baruch's great exhortation to the elders. The contrast between the passing world and the coming eternal reality (vv.5-7) is classically apocalyptic. The phrase "the Anointed One who was to come" (v.8) is significant — referring to a future Messiah from Israel's perspective.*
